dissent: An unconditional 'typed full-state restoration' claim is not supported by the supplied source: per-event binding is digest-only and the sole direct typed anchors are the terminal check and the transported-case comparison; the correct statement is the conditional invariant with P5/P6.

The F4 prediction (tuple->list masked when later overwritten) is conditional on canonical type-blindness, which cannot be decided from supplied sources; if canonical encodes type tags, the falsification boundary moves to pure collision/deletion cases.

Treating audit_case's re-audit of restored transitions as proof of equality with the historical execution implicitly assumes reducer determinism; the source asserts determinism per-run via inclusive/split agreement rather than proving it.
findings: Proof obligation (conditional invariant): for trace T with s0=initial and s(j+1)=apply(sj,events[j].patch), given (P1) len(events)=len(actions) with per-position action equality, uniqueness and requires-subset ordering (adapter_traces.py:62-64); (P2) digest(sj)=before_sha256 and digest(s(j+1))=after_sha256 (adapter_traces.py:65,71); (P3) per-prefix done bitmask equals executed-set sum (adapter_traces.py:71); (P4) adapter-only q_profile=subprofile(profile) and core.done equals actual-invocation mask (adapter_traces.py:72-74); (P5) canonical-injectivity including type distinctions; (P6) a terminal or per-prefix typed anchor: then exact(sj,executed_j) for all j.

Omitted fields: trace_event emits patch entries only for keys present in after (adapter_traces.py:54-58); restore never deletes keys (update-only: adapter_traces.py:67-69). A deleted field survives in the replay and is caught only by the after_sha256 mismatch; a new field instead raises KeyError at trace construction. Detection of omission is therefore digest-mediated, not structural.

Tuple/list loss: typed()/exact() is type-sensitive (semantic.py:14-18) while digest() hashes q.canonical (semantic.py:21), imported from q_domain (s_domain.py:10), which is absent from the supplied workspace (tool:1, tool:6). If canonical is type-blind (standard JSON), a tuple->list patch passes every per-event hash; the terminal exact check (adapter_traces.py:127) catches it only if the field is never overwritten later. artifact.encode/decode preserves tuple/list/Envelope tags (artifact.py:13-21); q_artifact.pack alone flattens tuples to lists (q_artifact.py:13), so transport fidelity requires the encode-before-pack ordering used in check.py.

Hash vs typed equality: restore performs zero typed comparisons; typed restoration is established only by (a) the terminal exact in run (adapter_traces.py:127) and (b) check.py's exact(case,restored) disk round-trip (check.py:193) plus deterministic replay. audit_case re-audits each restored transition (check.py:103-121) but never typed-compares intermediate restored states to executed states.

Chronological event binding: order is bound by per-position action equality, no-reexecution, requires-closure and the order-insensitive per-prefix done set (adapter_traces.py:62-71); incarnation pairs are bound to event indices by causality requires (adapter_traces.py: 'causal immutable incarnation ledger'; check.py:115-116). restore never requires actions to cover profile['actions'], so a truncated trace is restorable - completeness is generation-side only.

Falsifiable clauses: F1 drop/duplicate/reorder event -> reject (controls 'dropped-visible-adapter-event' adapter_traces.py:148, 'dropped-visible-event' check.py); F2 hash-visible patch corruption -> reject; F3 omitted after-state field -> reject iff canonical distinguishes dict cardinality; F4 tuple->list on a later-rewritten field -> ALL checks including terminal exact accept, falsifying any unconditional typed-restoration claim; F5 reordered q_profile -> reject ('moved-potential-Q-occurrence' adapter_traces.py:150); F6 forged pair event index -> reject.

Missing premises: canonical() semantics (tuple/list, bool/int, Envelope, floats) - unsupplied; SHA-256 collision resistance; reducer determinism (asserted per-run by inclusive/split agreement, not proved by restore); adapter core/journal dict-typed values; trace['initial'] fidelity (checked by initialization audits, not by restore); trace['side'] outside {'source','adapter'} silently takes source patch semantics.

Smallest decisive check (proposed, not executed): one in-memory history on the shortest profile; three mutations of the recorded trace - (i) tuple->list in a later-rewritten patch field, predict end-to-end acceptance; (ii) tuple->list in a never-rewritten field, predict terminal-exact rejection; (iii) one deleted after-state key, predict digest rejection. Outcome of (i) decides whether the invariant is 'typed' or only 'hash-bound plus terminal-typed'.

Scope: this concerns retained-trace integrity on executed histories (FOCUS=5 profiles or 104 packet-C cases; declared finite domains in check.py), not original-scale reachability - packets 04+08 cover 240/40320 orders per unit (remaining-scale-coverage-analysis.md; spec.json analytic 384 histories).
limitations: No execution performed: run_command, imports and reducer execution were prohibited; all restore behavior described is source inference, not observed output.
q_domain.py, q_audit.py, histories.py and the batch-07 manifest are absent from the supplied workspace; canonical, checked_payload, enabled and ACTIONS semantics are unverified.
Truncation coverage gap (restore accepts traces shorter than the profile) and malformed-state paths (non-dict core/journal, foreign 'side' values) are analyzed hypothetically, not exercised.
Analysis covers retained-trace integrity on already-executed histories only; it establishes nothing about all-order reachability or the pending 87-command gates.
summary: Source-only derivation of the typed full-state restoration invariant over retained patch traces. restore() enforces complete event inventory, per-position literal action equality, dependency order, per-event before/after SHA-256 binding and done-mask/Q-invocation-mask binding (adapter_traces.py:60-76), but patch application is update-only and per-event binding is hash-based, not typed; terminal typed equality is asserted only at adapter_traces.py:127 and transitively via check.py:193. The decisive unverified premise is q_domain.canonical type-sensitivity, whose source is not supplied.
